`nodejs.install` works with npm 12, and the `Router`'s CloudFront function leaves more room for your own injection. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

### Fixes

- **`nodejs.install` now works with npm 12.** A function that installs packages at build time failed on npm 12 with `EUNKNOWNCONFIG`, because npm 12 rejects flags it doesn't know and `--platform` and `--arch` were two of them. The install no longer passes `--platform` and `--arch`. It selects the function's platform with `--os=linux` and `--cpu=<x64|arm64>` (and `--libc=glibc` for `sharp`), as before, so native packages such as `esbuild` and `sharp` are still fetched for the function's architecture. npm 10 and 11 give the same result as before. npm older than 9.9 still completes the install, but installs the packages for the machine it runs on instead of the function's architecture, before and after this change. ([#122](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/122), [anomalyco/sst#7031](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7031), [anomalyco/sst#6946](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6946))

### Changes

- **A `Router` leaves about 1 KB more room for `edge.viewerRequest.injection`.** CloudFront limits the viewer-request function to 10,240 bytes, and the route lookup and the `cloudfront.net` block are now minified. On a test router with three sites, a URL route and a bucket route the function went from 8,872 to 7,898 bytes, and an injection of 1,800 bytes that CloudFront rejected as too large now deploys. The 403 that a request to the `cloudfront.net` URL gets, from a component that has a `domain` (`Router`, `StaticSite` or `SsrSite`) and from every `HttpsRedirect`, now has the plain text body `403 Forbidden` instead of an HTML page. Its status code and description are the same. `StaticSite` and `SsrSite` use the smaller block too, which saves them about 150 bytes; the rest of their function is unchanged. For a `Router`, the first deploy after you update changes the code of its viewer-request function in place and replaces nothing. It also runs the route data, file sync and CloudFront invalidation steps of the sites behind the `Router` again, so each `StaticSite` gets one invalidation. ([#124](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/124), [anomalyco/sst#7030](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7030))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.3
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.3"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
